intro.title: Memory Leak Hunt
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that demonstrates and fixes a common memory leak caused by an uncleaned-up interval timer. You'll learn how memory leaks occur when components don't properly clean up side effects like timers or event listeners after unmounting. The core concept involves using the useEffect hook to manage side effects and its cleanup function to prevent leaks. You'll work with React's useState for state management and setInterval for creating the timer. By the end, you'll understand how to write components that avoid memory leaks by cleaning up resources when they are no longer needed.
intro.usecase: Memory leak prevention is critical in long-running React applications like data dashboards and admin panels, where users keep tabs open for hours while monitoring live charts, tables, and filters. For example, a financial analytics dashboard might continuously fetch and display real-time stock data; if event listeners or intervals from old components aren't cleaned up, the app gradually consumes more memory, slowing down the browser and potentially crashing it. Developers implement cleanup in useEffect to handle component unmounting—ensuring that subscriptions, WebSocket connections, or timers are properly disposed of when a user navigates away from a chart or closes a modal, maintaining app performance and stability.
